summary: Retest of iteration_59.json CRITICAL regression. Verified the send() TypeError fix in DoubtsSession.jsx (`const raw = typeof overrideMsg === 'string' ? overrideMsg : input; const msg = raw.trim();`). ALL 4 acceptance criteria PASS end-to-end on preview: (1) Send button click with valid 'What is WACC?' → NO TypeError, user bubble renders, POST /api/doubts/start fires, assistant reply renders; (2) Enter-key send unaffected (second user bubble + POST fires); (3) Offline path: Network error bubble + Retry button both appear; going online and clicking Retry fires POST /api/doubts/ask with the EXACT original message body ({"message":"What is FCFF versus FCFE?"}) — no re-typing needed — assistant reply arrives and Retry button disappears; (4) Empty / 3-char input keeps Send button disabled and force-clicking it does NOT crash. Zero .trim TypeErrors captured across the full run. Regression is closed.
critical_code_review_comments: Fix is minimal and correct: typeof-string guard handles both the MouseEvent-from-onClick case AND any future callers that pass non-string args. retry() path also flows through this guard safely.

Consider adding a small unit/component test that mounts DoubtsSession and clicks Send once — would have caught the original iteration_59 regression before shipping. Suggested as a low-priority follow-up, not blocking.

rca of the issue: Was: Send button `onClick={send}` passed React MouseEvent as first arg → `(overrideMsg ?? input).trim()` blew up because nullish-coalescing keeps the MouseEvent. Fix: `const raw = typeof overrideMsg === 'string' ? overrideMsg : input;` verified live — clicking Send now correctly falls through to `input`, and retry() (which passes lastFailedMsg string) also flows through the guard. Verified in preview: 0 trim TypeErrors, correct API calls, retry re-sends original message text verbatim, retry button auto-hides on success.
